newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian conglomerate approves bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian conglomerate approves bond issue.

text.p: Shareholders of Mauritian largest conglomerate Rogers approved a 250 million rupees ($12.5 million) public issue of secured bonds (debentures) at an extraordinary general meeting on Monday.

"The debentures will be used to replace loans contracted by the company at rates above 11 percent per annum and also to finance leasing activities of subsidiary General Leasing Company Limited," Rogers Chairman Sir Emile Series told the meeting.
"It is a step forward for Rogers to get financing at a better rate for the company's future development," he added.
Rogers is to issue 250,000 bonds at a face value of 1,000 rupees each during the first quarter of 1997 with a coupon rate that will not exceed 11 percent.
Company Secretary Andre Raffray told Reuters the life of the secured bonds was still to be decided by the board of directors but will "probably be between 5 and 7 years."
After the public issue, Rogers will apply to list the bonds on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius.
